question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation feature with model-facing continuation/delegate/compaction tools, durable TaskFlow queues, and trusted cross-session delegate returns when `crossSessionTargeting` is enabled?
rationale: The code can be repaired mechanically, but the permanent product/security contract belongs to maintainers because it creates new core model authority, persisted state, config defaults, and cross-session context injection semantics.

options.title: Accept after gates pass
options.body: Resolve `native-i18n`, keep proof current at the merge head, and land with the current default-deny cross-session policy plus explicit maintainer acceptance of trusted targeted returns.

options.title: Narrow first release
options.body: Land only self-session continuation/delegate/compaction first and defer cross-session targeted trusted returns until a smaller follow-up decision.

options.title: Pause core integration
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers decide the feature is too broad for core or should be redesigned around a narrower plugin/API surface.

recommendation.title: Accept after gates pass
recommendation.body: Resolve `native-i18n`, keep proof current at the merge head, and land with the current default-deny cross-session policy plus explicit maintainer acceptance of trusted targeted returns.
